question: Who has been signed on as a brand ambassador of lubricant manufacturer Gulf Oil India in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smriti Mandhana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In October 2022, Gulf Oil Lubricants India Ltd. signed Indian women's cricket team star Smriti Mandhana as its brand ambassador. (गल्फ ऑयल इंडिया — स्मृति मंधाना)

 

• The tie-up was aimed at promoting Gulf Oil's lubricant products and strengthening its association with sports, aligning the brand with Mandhana's image as a dynamic, high-performing sportsperson.

 

• Smriti Mandhana is an opening batter for the Indian women's cricket team and has represented India in ODIs, T20Is and Tests; she has also captained the Indian women's team.

 

• Gulf Oil International is a global lubricants brand with operations in India through Gulf Oil Lubricants India Ltd., part of the Hinduja Group.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Brands frequently rope in top athletes as ambassadors to boost visibility; other companies have separately partnered with cricketers like Rishabh Pant and badminton players like Saina Nehwal for different campaigns, which is unrelated to this specific Gulf Oil deal.

 

NOTE

 

• Sonu Sood (Option 1): An actor known for his philanthropic work during the COVID-19 pandemic; not associated with this Gulf Oil campaign.

 

• Rishabh Pant (Option 2): An Indian men's cricketer; he was not the one signed by Gulf Oil India as brand ambassador in October 2022.

 

• Sania Nehwal (Option 3): The name refers to badminton player Saina Nehwal; she was not associated with this specific Gulf Oil endorsement.

question: The motion of the body moving along a circular path is an example of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is accelerated motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A body moving along a circular path continuously changes its direction of velocity, even if its speed remains constant. (वृत्तीय गति — त्वरित गति)

 

• Since acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity (a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction), any change in direction constitutes acceleration — this is why circular motion is always accelerated motion, called centripetal acceleration, directed towards the centre of the circle.

 

• This acceleration arises even in uniform circular motion (constant speed), because the direction of the velocity vector keeps changing at every instant.

 

• The force responsible for this acceleration is the centripetal force, which acts along the radius towards the centre of the circular path.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The magnitude of centripetal acceleration is given by a = v²/r, where v is speed and r is the radius of the circular path.

 

• Examples of circular motion include the motion of the Earth around the Sun, a stone tied to a string being whirled, and a vehicle turning around a circular curve.

 

NOTE

 

• Decelerated motion (Option 1): This refers to motion where speed is decreasing, which is not a defining characteristic of circular motion.

 

• Non-uniform motion (Option 3): This describes motion where speed changes with time; circular motion at constant speed is technically termed accelerated (due to direction change), not non-uniform in the speed sense.

 

• Uniform motion (Option 4): This term applies to motion in a straight line at constant velocity with zero acceleration, which circular motion never satisfies since direction is always changing.

question: Which of the following bills can be initiated only in the Lok Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Money bill.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 109 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and not in the Rajya Sabha. (धन विधेयक — केवल लोकसभा)

 

• A Money Bill can only be introduced on the recommendation of the President and only by a Minister.

 

• After passage in the Lok Sabha, the bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, which can only recommend changes (not reject or amend) and must return it within 14 days, failing which it is deemed passed.

 

• Whether a bill is a Money Bill or not is decided solely by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and that decision is final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 110 defines what constitutes a Money Bill — it must deal exclusively with matters like taxation, government borrowing, or the Consolidated Fund of India.

 

• Ordinary/Government bills and Constitution Amendment Bills (Article 368) can be introduced in either House of Parliament.

 

NOTE

 

• Private members bill (Option 1): Can be introduced in either House by any Member of Parliament who is not a minister.

 

• Constitution amendment bill (Option 2): Under Article 368, such a bill can be introduced in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Government bill (Option 3): An ordinary government bill (other than a Money Bill) can be introduced in either House of Parliament.

question: Where does the headquarters of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research Institute located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has its headquarters at New Delhi. (भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद — नई दिल्ली)

 

• ICAR was established on 16 July 1929 as a registered society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, following the recommendations of the Royal Commission on Agriculture.

 

• It is an autonomous organisation under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India.

 

• ICAR is the apex body coordinating, guiding and managing agricultural research and education across India, and it oversees a large network of research institutes and agricultural universities nationwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• ICAR has played a pivotal role in India's agricultural development, including the Green Revolution, through path-breaking research in crop varieties, livestock and fisheries.

 

• Premier institutes under ICAR include the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI, Pusa, New Delhi) and the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI, Karnal).

 

NOTE

 

• Amritsar (Option 1): Not the headquarters of ICAR; known instead for institutions like Guru Nanak Dev University.

 

• Surat (Option 2): Not associated with ICAR's headquarters; a major commercial and textile city in Gujarat.

 

• Lucknow (Option 3): Not the headquarters of ICAR, though it hosts some ICAR-affiliated institutes such as the Central Drug Research Institute area; the apex body itself is headquartered in New Delhi.

question: From which year did Sangeet Natak Akademi, New Delhi, institute the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, instituted the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar in the year 2006. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खां युवा पुरस्कार — 2006)

 

• The award is named in honour of the legendary shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan, a Bharat Ratna recipient.

 

• It is conferred annually on young, talented artists (below 40 years of age) in the fields of music, dance, drama, and other traditional/folk performing arts, to encourage and support emerging talent.

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and is the oldest of the National Akademis of Letters, Fine Arts and Performing Arts set up by the Republic of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1952 and also confers the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar).

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour, for his contribution to Hindustani classical music through the shehnai.

 

NOTE

 

• 2001 (Option 1): This is the year Ustad Bismillah Khan received the Bharat Ratna, not the year the Yuva Puraskar named after him was instituted.

 

• 2005 (Option 2): Not the correct year of institution of this award.

 

• 2004 (Option 3): Not the correct year of institution of this award.

question: Which of the following are food preservatives?
option_1: Salt, sodium nitrite, spices and vinegar
option_4: Formic acid, vinegar and methyl alcohol
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salt, sodium nitrite, spices and vinegar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Food preservatives are substances added to food to prevent or delay spoilage caused by microbial growth or unwanted chemical changes. (खाद्य परिरक्षक — नमक, सोडियम नाइट्राइट, मसाले, सिरका)

 

• Common salt (sodium chloride) preserves food by drawing out moisture through osmosis, inhibiting microbial growth (used in pickles, salted fish, etc.).

 

• Sodium nitrite is widely used to preserve processed/cured meats (like sausages and bacon), preventing bacterial growth, particularly *Clostridium botulinum*.

 

• Spices (like turmeric, clove) and vinegar (acetic acid) have natural antimicrobial properties and lower the pH of food, both of which help preserve it, as seen commonly in pickles and preserves.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common preservatives include sugar (used in jams and jellies), citric acid, sodium benzoate, and potassium metabisulphite.

 

• Preservation methods can be broadly classified as chemical (using preservatives), physical (drying, refrigeration, canning), and biological (fermentation).

 

NOTE

 

• Gypsum, soda and methyl alcohol (Option 2): Gypsum (calcium sulphate) is used in construction/plaster and food-grade applications like tofu coagulation, not as a general-purpose preservative; methyl alcohol is toxic and not a food preservative.

 

• Gypsum, salt and formic acid (Option 3): While salt is a preservative, gypsum and formic acid combined with it does not constitute the standard set of common food preservatives.

 

• Formic acid, vinegar and methyl alcohol (Option 4): Methyl alcohol (methanol) is toxic and unsafe for consumption, so this combination is incorrect as a set of food preservatives.

question: Who among the following was conferred with the Padma Shri Award, 2021, for populating folk dance in rural Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Matha B Manjamma Jogati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Matha B. Manjamma Jogati, a transgender folk artist, was conferred the Padma Shri Award in 2021 for her contribution to popularising Jogati folk dance/nritya in rural areas of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. (पद्म श्री 2021 — मंजम्मा जोगती)

 

• She received the award from President Ram Nath Kovind, and a photograph of her bowing to touch his feet before receiving the award went viral.

 

• Manjamma Jogati later became the first transgender person to head the Karnataka Janapada Academy (folk arts academy), being appointed its president in 2021.

 

• Her life story, marked by early hardships, is documented in the widely acclaimed autobiography 'Nadidhu Nudidhu' (I Danced, I Spoke).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, conferred by the President for distinguished contribution in various fields including art, literature, and social work.

 

• The Padma Awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri) are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.

 

NOTE

 

• Rama Swamy Annavarapu (Option 1): Not the recipient associated with this specific folk-dance-related Padma Shri citation.

 

• P Anitha (Option 2): Not the individual honoured for this specific folk dance contribution.

 

• Pappammal (Option 3): A centenarian organic farming expert from Tamil Nadu who received the Padma Shri, but for her contribution to organic farming, not folk dance.

question: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vijayalaya, the founder of the imperial Chola dynasty, built a temple for the goddess Nishumbhasudini (a form of Durga who slew the demon Nishumbha) at Thanjavur (Tanjore) after capturing it from the Muttaraiyar chieftains around the mid-9th century CE. (निशुम्भसूदिनी मंदिर — विजयालय चोल)

 

• This event, recorded in the Tiruvalangadu copper plates, is regarded as marking the founding moment of the resurgent Chola line after their earlier eclipse under Pallava and Pandya dominance.

 

• Vijayalaya's dynasty went on to become one of the greatest empires of South India, later reaching its zenith under his descendants.

 

• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its administrative system, maritime trade, and monumental Dravidian temple architecture, later exemplified by structures like the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aditya I, Vijayalaya's son, expanded Chola power by defeating the Pallavas and building numerous Shiva temples along the Kaveri river.

 

• Rajaraja I (r. 985-1014 CE) built the magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and greatly expanded the Chola empire including a naval campaign against Sri Lanka.

 

NOTE

 

• Aditya I (Option 1): Son of Vijayalaya, known for defeating the Pallava king Aparajita and building temples along the Kaveri, not for the Nishumbhasudini temple.

 

• Rajendra II (Option 2): A later Chola ruler, known for continuing conflicts with the Chalukyas; not associated with founding the Nishumbhasudini temple.

 

• Rajaraja I (Option 4): Renowned for constructing the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur and for major military expansion, not for the Nishumbhasudini temple, which predates his reign.

question: Which of the following line separates Pakistan and Afghanistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Durand line.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Durand Line is the international border separating Pakistan and Afghanistan, stretching about 2,670 km. (डूरंड रेखा — पाकिस्तान-अफगानिस्तान)

 

• It was established in 1893 through an agreement between Sir Henry Mortimer Durand, a British diplomat and civil servant, and the then Emir of Afghanistan, Abdur Rahman Khan.

 

• The line was originally demarcated to define the boundary between British India and Afghanistan, and after independence, Pakistan inherited it as its western border.

 

• The Durand Line cuts through Pashtun and Baloch tribal areas, and its legitimacy has historically been a subject of dispute, with Afghanistan not formally recognising it as an international border.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The McMahon Line (1914) separates India and China (in the eastern sector, Arunachal Pradesh), named after Sir Henry McMahon.

 

• The Radcliffe Line (1947), drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, demarcates the border between India and Pakistan.

 

NOTE

 

• McMohan line (Option 1): This refers to the McMahon Line, which separates India and China, not Pakistan and Afghanistan.

 

• Jinnah line (Option 2): Not a recognised international boundary line; this is a distractor name.

 

• Radcliffe line (Option 4): This is the boundary between India and Pakistan, drawn during the 1947 Partition, not between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

question: The Phase –I programme of ‘Sagar Parikrama’ has been organized in Gujarat, started on 5th March, 2022 from _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandvi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sagar Parikrama, an initiative of the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, aims to spread awareness about the socio-economic welfare of fishermen and highlight the importance of the Blue Economy. (सागर परिक्रमा — मांडवी, गुजरात)

 

• Its Phase-I programme was flagged off in Gujarat on 5th March 2022, beginning the journey from Mandvi and concluding the following day at Porbandar.

 

• The initiative was launched under the leadership of Union Minister Parshottam Rupala as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations.

 

• Subsequent phases of Sagar Parikrama were later carried out along the coastlines of other states, covering the country's vast maritime and fishing communities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sagar Parikrama supports the goals of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), aimed at the sustainable and responsible development of the fisheries sector.

 

• Later phases of Sagar Parikrama covered coastal states such as Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kheda (Option 1): A district in Gujarat, but not the starting point of Sagar Parikrama Phase-I.

 

• Porbandar (Option 2): This was the endpoint (day 2 destination) of the Phase-I leg, not its starting point.

 

• Banaskantha (Option 3): A district in Gujarat, not connected with the launch point of this programme.

question: Who was Player of the Match in the final of U-19 World Cup cricket,2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raj Bawa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2022, held in the West Indies, defeating England in the final. (अंडर-19 विश्व कप 2022 — राज बावा)

 

• All-rounder Raj Bawa was named Player of the Match in the final for his outstanding performance — he scored an unbeaten 35 runs and took 5 wickets for 31 runs.

 

• The Indian team was captained by Yash Dhull in this tournament, and this was India's record 5th U-19 World Cup title.

 

• The final was played at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium, Antigua, in February 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raj Bawa also finished as the tournament's second-highest run-scorer.

 

• India has won the U-19 World Cup in 2000, 2008, 2012, 2018, and 2022, more titles than any other nation.

 

NOTE

 

• James Rew (Option 1): A wicketkeeper-batter who played for England in this tournament, but not the Player of the Match in the final.

 

• Nishant Sindhu (Option 2): A member of the Indian squad in this tournament, but not adjudged Player of the Match in the final.

 

• Yash Dhull (Option 4): He was the captain of the victorious Indian team, but the Player of the Match award for the final went to Raj Bawa.

question: Warren Hastings became the first Governor General of India in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1773.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of India under the provisions of the Regulating Act of 1773, passed by the British Parliament. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट 1773 — वारेन हेस्टिंग्स)

 

• The Regulating Act, 1773 converted the post of Governor of Bengal into that of Governor-General of Bengal, with the Presidencies of Bombay and Madras placed under its control.

 

• Warren Hastings had earlier served as the Governor of Bengal from 1772, and became the first Governor-General under the new Act.

 

• He held this position until 1785 and played a key role in shaping early British administration in India, including judicial and revenue reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Later, under the Government of India Act, 1833, the post was upgraded to 'Governor-General of India', with Lord William Bentinck becoming the first holder of that specific title.

 

• The last Governor-General of India was C. Rajagopalachari, who held office after India became a republic-in-transition, until 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• 1767 (Option 1): Not connected with Warren Hastings' appointment; this predates the Regulating Act.

 

• 1757 (Option 2): This is the year of the Battle of Plassey, which established British political power in Bengal, not the year Hastings became Governor-General.

 

• 1783 (Option 4): Not the year of Hastings' appointment as Governor-General; he was already holding the post by this time and left office in 1785.

question: When expenditure exceeds revenue, the budget is said to be in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A budget deficit occurs when a government's total expenditure exceeds its total revenue in a given financial year. (राजकोषीय घाटा — बजट व्यय > राजस्व)

 

• To cover this deficit, the government typically resorts to borrowing (through market loans, treasury bills, etc.) or draws upon its reserves.

 

• The most commonly cited measure in India is the Fiscal Deficit, defined as total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.

 

• A large or persistent deficit can affect a country's macroeconomic stability, inflation, and credit rating, so governments aim to manage it within sustainable limits, often guided by targets under the FRBM Act, 2003.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A budget surplus is the opposite situation — when revenue exceeds expenditure.

 

• Other key deficit concepts in Indian public finance include the Revenue Deficit (excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts) and the Primary Deficit (fiscal deficit minus interest payments).

 

NOTE

 

• Surplus (Option 2): This describes the opposite condition, where revenue exceeds expenditure, not where expenditure exceeds revenue.

 

• Reserve (Option 3): Refers to funds set aside/saved, not a term describing an expenditure-revenue imbalance.

 

• Debt (Option 4): Refers to the total accumulated borrowing/liability of the government over time, which is a consequence of running deficits, but is not itself the term for the specific condition described.

question: Who wrote the book titled ‘Gift to Monotheism’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaram Mohan Rai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Gift to Monotheists' (originally titled 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' in Persian, meaning "A Gift to Monotheists") was written by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1803-04. (तोहफत-उल-मुवाहिद्दीन — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• In this treatise, Raja Ram Mohan Roy argued against idol worship and advocated the principle of monotheism (belief in one God), drawing on Hindu, Islamic and Christian philosophical traditions.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' and founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, a reform movement promoting monotheism and social reforms like the abolition of Sati.

 

• He was also instrumental in campaigning against practices like Sati, which was formally abolished through the efforts of Lord William Bentinck in 1829.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 and authored 'Satyarth Prakash'.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen was a prominent leader associated with the Brahmo Samaj, later founding the Brahmo Samaj of India and then the Church of the New Dispensation.

 

NOTE

 

• Swami Vivekanand (Option 1): A key disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, founder of the Ramakrishna Mission, not the author of 'Gift to Monotheists'.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 2): Author of 'Satyarth Prakash' and founder of Arya Samaj, not the author of this particular work.

 

• Kehsavchand Sen (Option 3): A Brahmo Samaj reformer, but not the author of 'Gift to Monotheists'.

question: Yamini Krishnamurthy is famous for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy was a celebrated Indian classical dancer, renowned primarily for her mastery of Bharatanatyam, and she also performed Kuchipudi. (यामिनी कृष्णमूर्ति — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She trained under legendary gurus, including Kanchipuram Ellappa Pillai for Bharatanatyam and Vempati Chinna Satyam for Kuchipudi.

 

• She received numerous honours, including the Padma Shri (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001), and Padma Vibhushan (2016), in recognition of her contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

• She founded the Yamini School of Dance in New Delhi to train future generations of classical dancers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is considered one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, traditionally performed in temples.

 

• Notable Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale and Padma Subrahmanyam, among others.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 1): A classical dance form from Manipur; noted exponents include the Jhaveri sisters, not Yamini Krishnamurthy's primary form.

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance form from Odisha; noted exponents include Sonal Mansingh and Kelucharan Mohapatra, not Yamini Krishnamurthy's main dance style.

 

• Yakshagana (Option 4): A traditional theatre form combining dance, music and dialogue from coastal Karnataka, not associated with Yamini Krishnamurthy.

question: What is the set of ecosystem called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Biome.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Biome is a large geographical region characterised by a specific climate, and by the distinctive plant and animal communities (ecosystems) adapted to it — essentially, a collection or set of ecosystems sharing similar ecological conditions. (बायोम — पारिस्थितिकी तंत्रों का समूह)

 

• Biomes are typically classified based on temperature, rainfall, soil type and vegetation, such as tropical rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, and taiga biomes.

 

• Within a single biome, multiple ecosystems (which are localised interacting units of living organisms and their physical environment) can exist together, sharing common broad climatic features.

 

• The concept of biome is important in ecology and biogeography for classifying and studying Earth's biodiversity at a large scale.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Earth's major biomes include: tropical rainforest, savanna, desert, temperate grassland, temperate forest, taiga (boreal forest), and tundra.

 

• The sum total of all ecosystems on Earth constitutes the biosphere, the global ecological system integrating all living beings and their relationships.

 

NOTE

 

• Stratosphere (Option 1): A layer of the Earth's atmosphere located above the troposphere, unrelated to grouping ecosystems.

 

• Hydrosphere (Option 2): Refers to all the water present on, under and above the surface of the Earth, not a grouping term for ecosystems.

 

• Atmosphere (Option 4): The layer of gases surrounding the Earth, not a term describing a collection of ecosystems.

question: Who choreographed the Bollywood song ‘Mohe Rang Do Laal’ from Bajirao Mastani?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birju Maharaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, the legendary Kathak exponent, choreographed the song 'Mohe Rang Do Laal' from the film 'Bajirao Mastani' (2015), directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali. (मोहे रंग दो लाल — पंडित बिरजू महाराज)

 

• He also choreographed other iconic dance sequences in the film, including 'Deewani Mastani', both showcasing intricate Kathak footwork and expressions.

 

• Birju Maharaj was a doyen of the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana of Kathak and received numerous honours, including the Padma Vibhushan (1986).

 

• Beyond Bajirao Mastani, he had earlier choreographed classic dance sequences in films such as 'Devdas' (2002) and 'Umrao Jaan' (1981).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj passed away in January 2022; he was widely regarded as one of the greatest exponents of Kathak of his generation.

 

• 'Bajirao Mastani' starred Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone and Priyanka Chopra, and won multiple awards for its music and choreography.

 

NOTE

 

• Saroj Khan (Option 1): A veteran Bollywood choreographer famed for numerous iconic dance numbers, but not the choreographer of this particular song.

 

• Farah Khan (Option 2): A well-known choreographer and director, but not associated with choreographing this song.

 

• Ganesh Acharya (Option 3): A prominent Bollywood choreographer, but he did not choreograph 'Mohe Rang Do Laal'.

question: Which of the following is a strong reducing agent used to reduce aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids and even carboxylate salts to alcohols?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lithium aluminum hydride.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lithium Aluminium Hydride (LiAlH₄) is a very strong and versatile reducing agent widely used in organic chemistry to reduce aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids, and even carboxylate salts to their corresponding alcohols. (लीथियम एल्युमिनियम हाइड्राइड — प्रबल अपचायक)

 

• It works by delivering a hydride ion (H⁻) to the electrophilic carbon of the carbonyl group, converting it into an alkoxide, which upon aqueous workup yields the alcohol.

 

• LiAlH₄ is a much stronger reducing agent compared to sodium borohydride (NaBH₄), and unlike NaBH₄, it can reduce carboxylic acids and esters efficiently.

 

• It must be handled carefully as it reacts violently with water and moisture, releasing flammable hydrogen gas, so reactions are typically carried out in anhydrous ether solvents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium borohydride (NaBH₄) is a milder reducing agent, generally used to selectively reduce aldehydes and ketones without affecting esters or carboxylic acids.

 

• LiAlH₄ can also reduce nitriles and amides to primary amines, showcasing its broad utility in synthetic organic chemistry.

 

NOTE

 

• Titanium hydride (Option 1): Mainly used in metallurgy and as a foaming agent/hydrogen storage material, not as an organic reducing agent for these functional groups.

 

• Calcium hydride (Option 3): Commonly used as a drying agent to remove trace moisture from solvents, not as a reducing agent for these carbonyl compounds.

 

• Bismuth hydride (Option 4): Not a standard or practically used reducing agent for such organic transformations.

question: The headwaters of the river Ganga is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagirathi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bhagirathi river is considered the headwaters (source stream) of the Ganga, originating at Gaumukh, at the snout of the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand. (भागीरथी — गंगा का उद्गम)

 

• At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda river, and from this confluence onward the combined river is officially known as the Ganga.

 

• The name Bhagirathi is associated with the legend of King Bhagiratha, who is said to have performed penance to bring the celestial river Ganga down to Earth.

 

• The Ganga basin is one of the most significant river systems in India, supporting a large population across the Indo-Gangetic plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Alaknanda river originates from the Satopanth glacier, and is joined by tributaries like the Mandakini (from Kedarnath) at Rudraprayag before meeting the Bhagirathi at Devprayag.

 

• India follows the Panch Prayag concept — five sacred confluences (Vishnuprayag, Nandprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, Devprayag) along the Alaknanda in Uttarakhand.

 

NOTE

 

• Mandakini (Option 1): A tributary that originates near Kedarnath and joins the Alaknanda at Rudraprayag, not the headwaters of the Ganga itself.

 

• Alaknanda (Option 2): One of the two headstreams that combine at Devprayag to form the Ganga, but it is the Bhagirathi that is traditionally regarded as the true source stream/headwaters.

 

• Sursari (Option 4): An alternate poetic/Sanskrit name sometimes used for the Ganga itself, not specifically referring to its headwaters.

question: In hockey, what is the meaning of the signal if the umpire points both arms horizontally towards the goal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Penalty corner.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In field hockey, when the umpire raises both arms horizontally and points them towards the goal, the signal indicates a penalty corner. (पेनल्टी कॉर्नर — दोनों हाथ क्षैतिज)

 

• A penalty corner is awarded for a defensive infringement inside the shooting circle, or for an intentional foul by a defender in their defensive 23-metre area.

 

• During a penalty corner, the attacking team gets a set-piece opportunity to score, with the ball restarted from a marked spot on the backline while defenders retreat behind the halfway line.

 

• Umpires in hockey use a standardised set of hand signals, prescribed by the International Hockey Federation (FIH), to communicate different decisions clearly to players and spectators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A goal is signalled by the umpire pointing towards the centre of the field/halfway line.

 

• A penalty stroke is signalled differently, typically by the umpire pointing directly at the penalty spot, and is awarded for a foul that denies a probable goal.

 

NOTE

 

• Free hit (Option 1): Signalled by the umpire raising one arm vertically, indicating the direction of the free hit, not by both arms horizontal towards the goal.

 

• Penalty stroke (Option 3): Signalled by the umpire pointing towards the penalty spot in front of the goal, a different gesture from raising both arms horizontally.

 

• Goal scored (Option 4): Signalled by the umpire pointing towards the centre of the field, not by pointing both arms towards the goal.

question: Government of India has appointed _______ as Controller General of Accounts in October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharati Das.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharati Das, a senior Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS) officer, took charge as the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) of India on 18 October 2022. (नियंत्रक महालेखाकार — भारती दास)

 

• She became the 27th Controller General of Accounts, functioning under the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

 

• The CGA is the apex accounting authority of the Central Government, responsible for establishing and maintaining a technically sound management accounting system, and for consolidating the Union Government accounts.

 

• The office of CGA also prepares and submits monthly and annual analyses of government expenditure and receipts to the Finance Ministry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Controller General of Accounts was established in 1976 as part of the departmentalisation of Government accounts, separating accounting functions from the Comptroller and Auditor General's audit role.

 

• The CGA also acts as an advisor on accounting matters to the various Ministries/Departments of the Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Vinayak Godse (Option 1): Not the person appointed as CGA in October 2022; he is associated with other administrative/policy roles.

 

• Sandeep Bakshi (Option 2): He is known as the MD & CEO of ICICI Bank, unrelated to the CGA appointment.

 

• KG Mohan (Option 4): Not the officer appointed as Controller General of Accounts in October 2022.

question: Low annual range of temperature and high annual rainfall are characteristics of a _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is tropical humid climate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A tropical humid (equatorial) climate is characterised by a low annual range of temperature (since areas near the equator receive fairly uniform, intense solar radiation year-round) and high annual rainfall (often exceeding 200 cm, well-distributed throughout the year). (उष्णकटिबंधीय आर्द्र जलवायु — कम तापांतर, अधिक वर्षा)

 

• Such regions lie roughly between 10°N and 10°S of the equator, and temperatures typically remain high (around 25-30°C) throughout the year with minimal seasonal variation.

 

• The high and consistent rainfall, combined with warm temperatures, supports dense tropical evergreen (rainforest) vegetation, as seen in the Amazon basin, Congo basin, and parts of Southeast Asia and India's Western Ghats.

 

• The small diurnal and annual temperature range is a defining feature that distinguishes equatorial/tropical humid climates from climates at higher latitudes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A Mediterranean climate features hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters, seen around the Mediterranean Sea and similar latitudinal belts.

 

• A temperate climate typically has moderate temperatures with a distinct seasonal cycle, while a cold climate shows very low temperatures and a much higher annual temperature range, especially in continental interiors.

 

NOTE

 

• Mediterranean climate (Option 1): Characterised by dry summers and wet winters, not by uniformly high rainfall and low temperature range.

 

• Temperate climate (Option 2): Shows a moderate but still noticeable annual temperature range with seasonal variation, unlike the very low range seen in tropical humid regions.

 

• Cold climate (Option 4): Marked by a large annual temperature range (very cold winters, milder summers) and generally lower rainfall, the opposite of what is described.

question: In ancient times, the area to the south of the Ganga was known as______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magadha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In ancient India, the region lying to the south of the river Ganga (corresponding roughly to present-day southern Bihar) was known as Magadha. (मगध — गंगा के दक्षिण)

 

• Magadha was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of ancient India and rose to become the most powerful kingdom, eventually forming the core territory of great empires like the Haryanka, Nanda, Maurya, and Gupta dynasties.

 

• Its early capital was Rajgriha (Rajgir), later shifted to Pataliputra (modern Patna), which became one of the greatest cities of the ancient world under the Mauryas.

 

• Magadha's strategic location, fertile land, access to iron ore, and control of trade routes contributed significantly to its rise as the dominant power of the Gangetic plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous rulers of Magadha include Bimbisara and Ajatashatru of the Haryanka dynasty, and later Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire.

 

• Magadha's dominance eventually gave rise to the concept of a unified empire, with the Mauryan Empire under Ashoka covering most of the Indian subcontinent.

 

NOTE

 

• Kosala (Option 2): A Mahajanapada located to the north of the Ganga, with its capital at Shravasti/Ayodhya, associated with the legendary Ikshvaku dynasty.

 

• Anga (Option 3): A Mahajanapada located east of Magadha, roughly corresponding to parts of present-day Bihar and West Bengal, with its capital at Champa.

 

• Matsya (Option 4): A Mahajanapada located in the region of present-day Rajasthan (around Jaipur/Alwar), unrelated to the area south of the Ganga.

question: ________ port, situated at the head of Gulf of Kuctch has been developed as a major port to cater to the needs of western and north-western parts of the country and also to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kandla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kandla Port, located at the head of the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat, was developed as a major port to serve the needs of the western and north-western parts of India and to relieve congestion at Mumbai Port. (कांडला बंदरगाह — गुजरात, कच्छ की खाड़ी)

 

• It was built after independence, following the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan during Partition, becoming a key alternative gateway for trade in western India.

 

• Kandla is a major (tidal) port and has historically been known for handling large volumes of bulk cargo, petroleum products, and general cargo.

 

• It was later renamed Deendayal Port in 2017, in honour of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, and remains one of India's busiest ports by cargo volume.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has 12 major ports, including Kandla (Deendayal), Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva), Kolkata, Chennai, Vishakhapatnam, Cochin, Paradip, and others.

 

• The Gulf of Kutch, an inlet of the Arabian Sea, is significant for its rich marine biodiversity and was declared India's first Marine National Park.

 

NOTE

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 1): An inland city in Gujarat, not a port, and not located at the Gulf of Kutch.

 

• Kochchi (Option 3): Refers to Kochi (Cochin) Port, located on the south-western coast of India in Kerala, not at the Gulf of Kutch.

 

• Kolkata (Option 4): A major riverine port on the Hooghly river in West Bengal, serving eastern India, not the Gulf of Kutch region.

question: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act passed by the Indian Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1955.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Citizenship Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in the year 1955. (नागरिकता अधिनियम — 1955)

 

• This Act was enacted to provide detailed provisions for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship, supplementing the basic citizenship provisions already laid down in Part II (Articles 5-11) of the Constitution of India.

 

• The Act specifies various ways of acquiring citizenship: by birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation, and by incorporation of territory, and also lays down provisions for termination of citizenship.

 

• Since its enactment, the Citizenship Act, 1955 has been amended several times, including significant amendments in 1986, 2003, 2005, and 2019 (Citizenship Amendment Act, CAA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constitution of India came into effect on 26 January 1950, and its Articles 5 to 11 dealt with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

 

• The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 amended the 1955 Act to provide a path to citizenship for persecuted religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India before 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• 1950 (Option 1): This is the year the Constitution of India came into force, not the year the separate Citizenship Act was passed.

 

• 1945 (Option 2): Predates Indian independence and the Constitution; not the correct year for this Act.

 

• 1948 (Option 4): Not the year of enactment of the Citizenship Act; it predates the actual legislation passed in 1955.
